title: Zero-free Taylor polynomial conjecture for square roots of truncated geometric series
statement:
Let $d>2$ and define the coefficients $b_k^{(d)}$ by

$$
\sqrt{1+z+\cdots+z^d}=\sum_{k=0}^\infty b_k^{(d)}z^k.
$$

For each $n\geq 0$, the corresponding **partial sum** is the polynomial $\sum_{k=0}^n b_k^{(d)}z^k$. **Zero-free Taylor polynomial conjecture.** For $d>2$, every such partial sum has no zeros in $\overline{\mathbb D}$, where $\mathbb D$ is the open unit disk. This conjecture would extend the zero-free result established in the paper for $d=2$ and is relevant to sharp bounds for segments of bounded power series via the Landau–Szász method.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.04544

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).
source_name: Leonid V. Kovalev, “Sharp bounds for some segments of bounded power series”, arXiv:2507.04544 (2025).
